title: Florida House, District 9
what_it_does: Represents District 9 (Madison, Parts of Jefferson, Leon) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Tracy Robinson
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Artificial intelligence engineer; background in emergency management and law enforcement
candidates.background: Tracy Robinson of Madison is a Florida A&M University graduate who has worked in emergency management, law enforcement and technology, including as an artificial intelligence engineer. A first-time candidate, she describes herself as a 'community first' Republican and won the August 2026 primary over Jibri Knight.

other_issues.title: The REVIVE District 9 agenda
other_issues.summary: Robinson describes herself as a community first Republican and runs on what she calls the REVIVE agenda: restoring communities, expanding economic opportunity, investing in infrastructure, supporting veterans and public safety, strengthening education, and promoting faith and families. In the primary she emphasized community revitalization, economic development and bringing technology and innovation to state government. Her campaign site does not set out detailed positions on specific bills.

Tracy Robinson - Florida House District 9

other_issues.title: Names education and elder care as top priorities; says she declines some donations
other_issues.summary: At the Sept. 28, 2026 League of Women Voters of Tallahassee/Capital Region News Collaborative forum at WFSU Studios, Robinson said education would be one of her top priorities and pledged support for elder care. She described closed grocery stores, high gas prices and declining neighborhoods in the Madison area as evidence of the affordability problem, and said she has turned down donations that do not align with her party or the district.

candidates.name: Allison Tant
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Former chair of the Florida Democratic Party; nonprofit founder; state representative since 2020
candidates.background: Allison Tant was born in Jacksonville, earned degrees in communications and psychology from Florida State University, and chaired the Florida Democratic Party before winning the District 9 seat in 2020. She founded Keys to Exceptional Youth Success and Independence Landing, organizations serving people with disabilities, and serves as a Democratic deputy whip in the House.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted no on HJR 1-F (June 2, 2026) and HJR 203 (Feb. 19, 2026); she said local governments fear losing autonomy and being treated like wards of the state.
property_tax.quote: They're worried about loss of autonomy, independence, and losing their identity. They are worried about becoming wards of the state and essentially be treated like welfare recipients.

other_issues.title: Says her focus is affordability and district appropriations (Sept. 28 forum)
other_issues.summary: At a Sept. 28, 2026 candidate forum at WFSU Studios hosted by the Capital Region News Collaborative and the League of Women Voters of Tallahassee, Tant said affordability is the top issue in the race and pointed to appropriations she has secured for the district. She said young people leave the area because of a lack of jobs.
